theme: Turn human motives into movement: persuasion earns consent, stories create consequence, positions clarify choice, desire gives meaning, strategy finds the right market, growth removes friction, and writing makes the next step obvious.

days.fundamental: Persuasion: understand how shared identity can make a request feel self-consistent, then distinguish genuine belonging from manufactured in-group pressure.
days.fallback_acquire_note: Available locally and in Drive. This advances beyond the previously studied Cialdini Chapters 1-7; canon prep should verify the Chapter 8 boundary.

days.work: Story: Substance, Structure, Style, and the Principles of Screenwriting
days.fundamental: Storytelling: convert an intuition into a disciplined process of observing, structuring, revising, and testing choices against the story's controlling idea.
days.fallback_acquire_note: Available locally and in Drive. This is the next non-repeated McKee chapter after Chapter 12, The Text; canon prep must bound the scanned PDF to the verified chapter range.

days.work: Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind
days.fundamental: Positioning/brand: make a follower's offer legible by owning a credible alternative position instead of imitating the leader on the leader's terms.
days.fallback_acquire_note: Available locally and in Drive. This follows the already studied Chapter 6, Positioning of a Leader, and is the next distinct chapter.

days.chapter_or_section: Part II, Chapter 9, "The Third Technique of Breakthrough Copy: Gradualization"
days.fundamental: Human desire/psychology: move a skeptical prospect toward action by sequencing belief and desire in tolerable steps instead of demanding one giant leap.
days.fallback_acquire_note: Available locally and in Drive. This advances beyond the previously studied Part II Chapter 8, The Second Technique of Breakthrough Copy: Identification; canon prep must verify a bounded Chapter 9 section.

days.fundamental: Tech/strategy: treat an emerging market as a discovery problem whose size, customers, and product definition must be learned rather than forecast from an established market.

days.fundamental: Distribution/growth: make growth durable by finding the repeated value that brings users back, then use cohorts and experiments to remove the causes of early abandonment.

days.fundamental: Writing/taste: name the customer's external, internal, and philosophical problem precisely enough that the message creates recognition before it offers a solution.
